nodes.label: Post-Change Verification Rule
nodes.rationale: After every change, run npm run format && npm run lint && npm run type-check && npm run build and fix any errors before considering the work done, to keep the codebase consistently formatted, lint-clean, type-safe and buildable.

nodes.label: Feature Module Pattern (components/, types.ts, index.ts barrel)
nodes.rationale: Each feature module (auth, billing, customers, inventory, print-jobs, repairs, reports) shares the same shape and is imported only through its barrel (@/features/billing), not by reaching into components/, to keep module boundaries enforced.
nodes.norm_label: feature module pattern (components/, types.ts, index.ts barrel)

nodes.label: isBillingBoundaryChange Render-Time State Adjustment
nodes.rationale: Suppresses AppShell's Mantine transition for the one render where a billing-specific boundary (header height/navbar width/padding) is crossed, so an animated chrome resize doesn't land in the same frame as a heavy screen's first mount and appear stuck.

nodes.label: Animation Performance Rules
nodes.rationale: Derived from a real incident: navigating into Billing appeared to make the left navbar 'shrink' with a stuck animation. Root cause was AppShell's own chrome transition (driven by isBillingPage) racing Billing's heavy first mount, worsened by an unrelated left-property animation and an app-wide re-render fan-out. Rules: only animate transform/opacity (compositor-only), snap route/screen boundaries instead of animating them, never call useMediaQuery directly, and never pair a @keyframes animation with transition: all on the same element.

nodes.label: LayoutTierProvider
nodes.rationale: A single shared media-query subscription mounted once above the router, instead of ~40 independent useMediaQuery listeners, so one breakpoint crossing does not fire a synchronized re-render burst across the whole tree that collides with in-flight CSS transitions. Uses getInitialValueInEffect:false to avoid a first-frame flash of the wrong layout.

nodes.label: Responsive & Mobile UI Layout Tiers
nodes.rationale: The app targets three layout tiers (mobile <768px one region, tablet 768-1199px two columns with tab-switch, desktop 1200px+ full multi-column) derived from Mantine 9 default breakpoints, so every new screen must be tested and shaped around these tiers rather than ad hoc widths.

nodes.label: ConnectivityMonitor
nodes.rationale: navigator.onLine alone is not a connectivity signal (it only sees the link layer), so ConnectivityMonitor combines it with the apiClient interceptor's statusCode:0 signal and a GET /health probe, with asymmetric hysteresis: offline publishes immediately, online is held for a settle window.

nodes.label: localId.ts (Provisional local_ IDs)
nodes.rationale: Never invent a server-generated identity locally: sku, barcodes and every key/id come from the server; rows created offline get a provisional local_<uuid> id and the engine rewrites every reference to it at flush time.

nodes.label: vite-plugin-pwa Service Worker
nodes.rationale: Precaches the app shell so a reload during an outage doesn't show the browser offline page; registerType:'prompt' (never autoUpdate) because an update reload would drop the active cart; no runtimeCaching for /api so a cached 200 doesn't make a dead backend look online.

nodes.label: POST /sequences/{name}/reserve
nodes.rationale: Sequential human-facing numbers (INV-2026-0042, REP-…, PRT-…) are minted server-side at the moment a sale/repair/print-job is created, never client-side; a ticket created offline has no number until its create operation reaches the server.

nodes.label: Backend Sync Contract (Rust/Axum)
nodes.rationale: Every syncable collection soft-deletes (never hard-deletes) so a delta pull can see deletions; GET /sync/changes is one multiplexed delta endpoint so a reconnect is one round trip; GET /sync/status returns the cursor for the newest row since /sync/changes pages oldest-first; Idempotency-Key on every mutating request makes retrying a request whose response was lost to a power cut safe; If-Match/version gives 409 VERSION_CONFLICT; the server is the oversell authority via 409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK.

nodes.label: Offline & Sync Architecture
nodes.rationale: The shop loses internet regularly (power cuts, ISP outages), so the app is offline-first: every synced resource mirrors into IndexedDB via Dexie and the UI reads only that mirror; writes apply locally first and queue in a durable outbox flushed on reconnect.

nodes.label: Durable Outbox Pattern
nodes.rationale: Writes apply locally first and queue in a durable outbox table that flushes when connectivity returns; the outbox, idMap, conflicts and stockLedger tables hold data that exists nowhere else and must be migrated in place, never dropped.

nodes.label: initializeAuth (Offline Auth Grace Period)
nodes.rationale: Treats anything short of an outright 401/403 rejection as unverified rather than invalid: it restores the cached identity from Dexie and sets isOfflineSession with a 7-day grace period, since an unreachable server or a 500 from /auth/me doesn't mean the credentials went bad.

nodes.label: authSlice (login/loginSuccess cacheSession)
nodes.rationale: The session is cached on login as well as on a successful /auth/me; caching only in initializeAuth meant a cashier who logged in and then lost connectivity had nothing to restore from on the next reload.

nodes.label: A4InvoicePreviewModal.tsx
nodes.source_location: Center modals — one visual family / Keyboard shortcuts

nodes.label: Center Modal Visual Family
nodes.rationale: Every center-opening Modal follows ProductFormModal's pattern: plain-text no-icon title, no radius override (defaultRadius:'md' applies), centered + fullScreen={isMobile} except small confirm dialogs, standard footer (Cancel variant='default', primary action blue), uppercase section labels, and blue as the only brand accent (semantic colors like green/orange/red stay independent).

nodes.label: UI Copy — Plain Language Rule
nodes.rationale: The app's user is a non-technical, possibly non-native-English-speaking shop owner, so all user-facing text must avoid standards names/internals (EAN-13, GS1, SKU collision rules, delta, cursor, outbox, idempotency), developer/DB jargon (immutable, validation error, vendor, intake), must plainly state optionality and repeatability, and validation messages must say what to do rather than what failed.

nodes.label: invoices.resource.ts
nodes.rationale: Checkout is one compound server-side write (invoice + payment + stock decrement + ticket-delivery + customer-balance update) whose non-invoice side effects can each independently fail into a warnings[] list; localApply writes only the invoice row and stock deltas, and push requests unscoped follow-up pulls for payments/repairs/printJobs/customers rather than optimistically mirroring them.

nodes.label: stockLedger.ts (Local Delta Ledger)
nodes.rationale: Never store an absolute value for anything that accumulates: stock is the server's baseline plus a local delta ledger, since deltas commute across devices but absolute overwrites do not (two terminals each selling one unit must produce -1 and -1, not conflicting totals).

nodes.label: syncNotifications.ts
nodes.rationale: Sync toasts use a stable notification id with notifications.update() and are edge-triggered with bookkeeping at module scope in SyncProvider, since the engine is a singleton whose effect re-runs on every auth flip and twice under StrictMode; 'Saved to the server' fires only when the change had actually been waiting so online edits don't bury the user in toasts.

nodes.label: Right-Side Detail Drawer Visual Family
nodes.rationale: Every right-side entity detail drawer follows a standard shape: icon+title/subtitle header, hero identity card, 3-column metrics snapshot Grid, tabbed operations (Tabs.List grow), inline expandable Collapse actions, and a metadata + Delete/Close/Edit footer, so entity profile drawers look and behave consistently across features.
